name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No regular IAEA access; HEU unverified
summary: IAEA cannot verify Iran's highly enriched uranium; Trump says strikes could resume after new year without a deal
state: An IAEA report circulated in mid-November says Iran has ruled out regular monitoring for now, and that the agency cannot verify where Iran's highly enriched uranium is or conclude that no declared material has been diverted (Bloomberg via News Tribune, 15 Nov). Trump said he may resume strikes after the new year if there is no deal, while Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said enriched material will not leave Iran (Iran International, 23 Nov). No new strike on a nuclear site or NPT withdrawal was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: Iran's nuclear status shapes the risk of renewed strikes and wider Gulf disruption. Travellers to the region should follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: inspector access curtailed and credible strike threats; no strike on nuclear sites or NPT withdrawal

sources.title: News Tribune (Bloomberg) — Iran extends shutout of UN nuclear inspectors
Iran International — US weighs delaying Iran strikes despite Israeli pressure for military action

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
